system_thesis_interpretation: The proposal preserves the project thesis as a staged organism rather than attributing success to a single substrate. Ordinary public source actions create the only evidentiary roots; target-blind DREAM proposes local relations and prospective schemas; a deterministic lifecycle/SLEEP boundary alone can admit chronologically supported claims; text, graph, and a later per-life LoRA expose those claims; and a frozen goal-conditioned THINK controller constructs a bounded cited path before executing ordinary actions. The one-pack DEV scope properly isolates instrument validity, controller headroom, learned compilation, and parametric transport, and it explicitly withholds the on-policy edge required for flywheel credit. A passing CPU world would therefore establish only that a deterministic fluid/thermal instrument and its falsifiers exist. Passing gold, learned-text, or LoRA DEV gates would remain one-pack information-value observations, not evidence of developmental scaling, general learning, or a closed action--experience loop. This interpretation does not treat the current prose as an executable specification: substantial world, interface, runtime, resource, and model choices remain open and must not be silently selected by implementers.
graph_delta_interpretation: The intended stage order is CPU world/instrument -> frozen organism and memory contracts -> gold-thinker plus learned-text DEV -> conditional same-corpus LoRA DEV -> terminal human stop, with a claim firewall spanning every node. Conceptually, public source replay reaches target-blind DREAM, later source outcomes reach a noncognitive status comparator, supported atoms reach deterministic compilation, a read-only snapshot yields bounded local returns to THINK, and isolated target outcomes flow only to audit/scoring. That graph is scientifically sensible. It is not yet mechanically constructible. No bound source/module/entrypoint or supervisor workflow instantiates any node; the fluid/thermal DSL, renderer, source policy, target constructors, twin mapping, legal planner, scorer, exact Bayes prior, reader, lifecycle objects, snapshot store, and resource ledger have no exact paths or schemas. The edge RML_E_EVALUATION_ISOLATION runs from the downstream gold/text gate back to RML_CPU_WORLD_GATE while RML_E_CPU_PASS_TO_GOLD_TEXT_DEV runs forward, forming a cycle if edges encode reachability or predecessor requirements. Isolation should instead be a one-way edge from a disposable evaluation runtime to a sealed audit sink plus a run/skip equality assertion, not a dependency back into the CPU stage. The graph also leaves the reader/backend, provider runtime, LoRA trainer, source policy, target generator, and authority supervisor implicit, so the visibility and capability firewall cannot be derived from graph reachability. CPU implementation is blocked until those CPU-owned nodes, interfaces, paths, and the isolation-edge semantics are bound. Exact model-backed implementations may be frozen later only behind a new byte-bound pre-call release; the present broad ratification cannot safely authorize unspecified future bytes.
loop_delta_interpretation: RML_L_CPU_WORLD_VALIDATION is the only loop that could execute before model work, but its current inputs do not determine a program: 'fluid/thermal generator', 'structural target and necessity rules', 'public source schedule', 'many worlds', and 'registered budgets' are names rather than exact algorithms or numbers. It lacks the causal-program grammar and distribution, canonical action/state/outcome serialization, outcome-blind schedule, rejection rule, pair/target/cut cardinalities, seed namespaces, scoring aggregation, exact controller specification, native-context tokenization contract, artifact layout, and finite CPU ceiling needed to reproduce a pass. The common-deck loop correctly calls for byte-identical replay, fresh disposable target processes, read-only snapshots, and resource vectors, but does not bind THINK/DREAM prompts and schemas, replay bundle construction, operation/query/action/sample/token caps, gold-memory construction, target counts/cuts, baseline adapters, provider call identities, or failure semantics. The LoRA loop correctly rebuilds from one frozen corpus and distinguishes recognition-assisted from unaided reads, but rank/modules/dtype/optimizer/schedule/examples/tokens/steps/seeds, fixed-query metric, candidate construction, parser, adapter reset, call and hardware ceiling, and interrupted-training disposition are unspecified. None of the three loops defines the content-addressed phase manifests, CREATED-to-SEALED call states, fsync/atomic-rename discipline, quarantine behavior, exact-response recovery, INDETERMINATE rule, or crash-at-every-boundary test supplied by the bound protocol precedents. Thus the proposal is staged but not crash-resumable or resource-bounded as written. World mechanics can be developed after an exact CPU contract; model prompts, exact backends, baseline revisions, generation configs, and the LoRA recipe may be frozen after CPU development but before any model call only if a new reviewed, human-bound artifact makes them immutable and unreachable beforehand.
claim_delta_interpretation: The claim firewall is appropriate and should remain controlling. CPU outputs can support only deterministic instrument-conformance observations. Gold-thinker output can diagnose resolver and target geometry; learned-text output can diagnose whether target-independent compilation produces useful supported structure relative to honest external baselines; same-corpus LoRA can receive only associative transport credit, with recognition-assisted and unaided generation reported separately. None of these DEV outcomes supports a benchmark headline, population effect, developmental curve, post-native saturation, LoRA superiority, autonomous discovery, learned resolver, external validity, or flywheel. A future fixed-deck result still cannot earn the memory -> better evidence -> later memory -> later action clause. The retirement of symbolic/PCFL headline status is a design choice, not empirical evidence that RML succeeds. Because model, baseline, metric, and budget details are unbound, the present bytes cannot yet determine even a reproducible DEV gate value; claim linting must therefore label later observations only after those definitions are separately frozen.
visibility_matrix_interpretation: The four-by-four matrix expresses the central rule—THINK sees a current target and bounded memory return, DREAM sees target-blind source replay, SLEEP sees eligible source evidence but no evaluation data, and only offline audit sees hidden truth—but it is too coarse to enforce the rule. V_PUBLIC_LIFE_SLICE conflates current target state with source-life replay; V_SUPPORTED_MEMORY_AND_PROVENANCE conflates model-visible atom content, parent handles, internal status history, roots, support counts, and corpus metadata; and the hidden item combines generator program, proofs, target pairing, selection receipts, scorer output, and evaluation records. Missing stages include the environment engine, scripted source policy, target/twin generator, lifecycle comparator, common reader and each backend, candidate builder, compiler, LoRA trainer, provider runtime, evaluation process, artifact supervisor, and report path. These omissions leave target-conditioned catalogs, generator imports, scorer leakage, provider caches, timing/error channels, corpus metadata, adapter assignment, and cross-life state outside the Cartesian audit. There is also an interface conflict: the matrix says THINK may receive bounded public support handles, while the graph and reconciled plan say one local atom or NOT_FOUND and the PCFL precedent hides provenance. DREAM is described as reading eligible earlier memories and roots without a numeric reader/bundle cap. Before CPU implementation, bind separate canonical stores/taints, writer ownership, process/import boundaries, source-versus-evaluation event types, reader request/return bytes, and audit-only origins. Before model calls, expand the matrix field-by-field across the actual provider, reader, baseline, trainer, and target processes and run deliberate answer-injection, cache/timing, run/skip, and cross-life canary tests.
acceptance_test_interpretation: RML01 correctly requires exact sorted scope and predecessor enforcement, but cannot establish implementation exactness until a file/entrypoint/command manifest, executable staged workflow, authority checks, and the repaired acyclic graph are bound. RML02 covers the right world properties, yet 'many' worlds, exact cuts, program grammar, twin transform, target families, legal-plan budget, causal-growth statistic, and success aggregation are absent; its run/skip clause also needs a sealed source-state contract. RML03 correctly requires oracle headroom and shortcut resistance, but the accepted-world prior, Bayes controller, predictor feature sets/training protocol, pair count, target count, per-stratum aggregation, identification threshold, and selection-conditioned audit are not exact. RML04 has the right attacks, but needs field-level taint schemas, exclusive writers, process/import capability denial, exact lifecycle transitions, root equivalence, deliberate answer-injection sensitivity, phase manifests, crash recovery, and actual backend noninterference tests. RML05 is a valid component gate only after gold atoms/schema, nonadaptive/generic/program-search controllers, one-hop return, operation/action/query budgets, cut/target deck, score denominator, proof-credit checker, and mask/twin fork determinism are frozen. RML06 must bind every baseline's exact source revision and native interface, the common-channel condition, learned writer calls, resource ceilings, mandatory-arm failure policy, the formula for 70% of gold gain, and which endpoint/cuts determine the strongest baseline. RML07 must bind corpus identity, query deck, fidelity metric, assisted menu construction and hidden scan accounting, generative parser, LoRA training envelope, adapter seeds, one-cut selection rule, mean/noninferiority calculation, crash semantics, and maximum compute. RML08 correctly requires identical hashes and a non-overriding advocate, but the exact review bundle does not yet exist and review cannot substitute for human authorization of material model/budget choices not contained in the current proposal. RML09 correctly stops claims and external actions, but the firewall must be enforced from implementation onward, not only before a scientific claim, and must include workflow reachability plus terminal no-promotion receipts. In timing terms, CPU work is blocked by the missing world/interfaces/workflow/durability/resource contract. Model identities, prompts, baseline revisions, exact DEV decks, generation settings, and LoRA recipe may be chosen after CPU development only through a fresh freeze/review/ratification before the first applicable call; the tokenizer/prompt reserve defining L_native must be frozen before the CPU gate can certify its final lifetime cuts.
assumptions: The one-pack scope means fluid/thermal DEV only; power/control, material/biological, locked, additional-pack, scale, and on-policy work remain unreachable.
The phrase at most four DEV pairs in the reconciled plan is a ceiling rather than an executable sample-size choice; an exact count still has to be frozen.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The current proposal is not exact enough to release the CPU implementation atom without implementers choosing material benchmark and systems behavior.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: No fluid/thermal DSL, schemas, source schedule, target/twin algorithms, Bayes prior, scorer, cardinalities, paths, workflow, artifact contract, crash semantics, or CPU ceiling is bound. RML01's exact-scope promise therefore covers categories, not executable bytes.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Before CPU implementation authority, revise or supplement the proposal with a hash-bound CPU execution bundle containing the complete world and controller specification, canonical object schemas, file/command/workflow allowlist, seed/split/cardinality manifest, scoring/gate formulas, visibility/capability map, artifact/resume protocol, and finite CPU resource budget; then rerun deliberation and exact human ratification.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: A single ratification of the present bytes should not automatically authorize later gold/text or LoRA calls after unspecified models, prompts, baselines, decks, and budgets are selected during implementation.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: Those choices materially determine L_native, information visibility, controller behavior, baseline strength, resource use, gate values, and LoRA transport. Independent review of later bytes is necessary but does not itself provide the AGENTS.md human ratification of exact material scope.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Allow later choices to be frozen after CPU development only in one or more new predecessor-bound artifacts that name exact models/tokenizers/runtime, prompts/schemas, calls/decks/seeds, native baselines, metrics, resource ceilings, and LoRA recipe; require fresh review and exact human ratification before the first applicable model or training call. Freeze the tokenizer/prompt reserve earlier, before final CPU cut certification.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: RML_E_EVALUATION_ISOLATION should not point from the gold/text stage back to the CPU world node.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: Together with RML_E_CPU_PASS_TO_GOLD_TEXT_DEV it forms a cycle in what is otherwise described as a predecessor graph. Noninterference is a property of a disposable evaluation branch and sealed audit comparison, not a feedback dependency into the source-life generator.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Replace it with explicit SourceLifeSnapshot -> EvaluationClone -> AuditOnlySink edges, forbid every write-back edge, and test source suffix/state/corpus/adapter hashes for run versus skip without altering stage reachability.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The current four-item/four-stage visibility matrix is insufficient to support the proposal's claim that RML is leakage-safe.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: It omits the reader, candidate builder, provider, trainer, environment, source policy, target generator, lifecycle comparator, evaluation process, supervisor, and report path, while conflating distinct data with different authorities. It also conflicts on whether support handles reach THINK.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Bind a field-level Cartesian matrix over every real process and canonical store, with taint propagation, exclusive writer rules, import/capability denial, exact reader bytes, source/evaluation event separation, deliberate answer-injection sensitivity, and black-box cache/timing/error/cross-life tests on the actual backends before their use.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: The acceptance suite does not presently make the three loops crash-resumable or resource-aware.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: There is no crash-at-every-seal test, provider dispatch/recovery state machine, indeterminate-call rule, partial-directory quarantine, adapter-training resume rule, exact terminal marker, or numeric CPU/model/GPU/training envelope. Sealed manifests and resource vectors in prose do not define these behaviors.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Add a pre-implementation CPU artifact/resume invariant and a pre-call provider/training durability invariant, each with exact state transitions and fault injection, plus machine-validated CPU, call, token, wall, memory, storage, GPU, training, and retry ceilings that stop rather than relax or rerun.

disagreements_with_proposal.statement: RML05, RML06, and RML07 are labeled required_before scientific_claim even though RML05/RML06 must mechanically block LoRA execution and RML07 must terminate the transport stage; RML09's external-action firewall is also needed before implementation and every run, not only before a claim.
disagreements_with_proposal.rationale: The generic required_before label cannot express repeated GPU subgates, and no bound workflow compensates for it. A supervisor could satisfy schema validation while failing to enforce the intended gold/text-to-LoRA transition or early external-action prohibition.
disagreements_with_proposal.proposed_resolution: Bind an executable phase workflow whose transition guards reference exact manifest hashes and pass formulas, require RML05/RML06 before the first LoRA dispatch, make RML07 terminal with no promotion edge, and run the scope/external-action firewall at every entry and terminal state.
